title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL ACT ON THE PROMOTION OF PERSONS SCHEDULED FOR PROMOTION WHO WERE KILLED IN ACTION OR DIED IN THE LINE OF DUTY

ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL ACT ON THE PROMOTION OF PERSONS SCHEDULED FOR PROMOTION WHO WERE KILLED IN ACTION OR DIED IN THE LINE OF DUTY

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Special Act on the Promotion of Persons Scheduled for Promotion Who Were Killed in Action or Died in the Line of Duty and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Applications for Promotion)
(1) A person intending to apply for promotion under Article 4 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Persons Scheduled for Promotion Who Were Killed in Action or Died in the Line of Duty (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter such application is referred to as an "application for promotion" and such person as an "applicant") shall submit to the Minister of National Defense an application for promotion in attached Form 1, accompanied by the following documents:
1. A certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register of the person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty, or a certified copy of the removed family register (limited to cases where the relationship between the person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty and the applicant cannot be verified by a certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register);
2. Other documents capable of proving that the person for whom an application for promotion has been filed (hereinafter referred to as the "person for whom promotion is requested") is a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty.
(2) Upon receiving an application for promotion pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall verify a certified copy of the applicant's resident registration record through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That, where the applicant does not consent to such verification, the Minister shall require the applicant to attach the relevant copy.

Article 3 (Verification of Facts)
(1) Upon receipt of an application for promotion, the Minister of National Defense may direct the Chief of Staff of each service or the Commandant of the Marine Corps to verify the following facts in order to decide whether to promote the person for whom promotion is requested:
1. Whether the person for whom promotion is requested is a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty;
2. Whether the person for whom promotion is requested has been promoted pursuant to Article 30 (1) of the Military Personnel Management Act.
(2) The Chief of Staff of each service or the Commandant of the Marine Corps shall report the results of the verification of facts concerning the relevant person for whom promotion is requested to the Minister of National Defense within 30 days from the date of receipt of a direction under paragraph (1) from the Minister.

Article 4 (Review by an Officer Promotion Selection Board)
Where, in the course of verifying facts under Article 3, the Chief of Staff of each service or Commandant of the Marine Corps confirms that the rank to which the person for whom promotion is requested is to be promoted pursuant to the former part of Article 3 (2) of the Act is a general-grade officer rank, the Chief of Staff or Commandant shall have the matter reviewed by an officer promotion selection board pursuant to the latter part of that paragraph and report the results together with the results of fact verification under Article 3 (2).

Article 5 (Decisions on Promotion)
The decisions on promotion that the Minister of National Defense may make with respect to a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty shall be as follows:
1. A decision on promotion under Article 3 (1) of the Act (including a decision setting the day before the date of death as the effective date of promotion pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Act);
2. A decision on promotion under Article 3 (2) of the Act. In such cases, the effective date of promotion to the next rank shall be the date on which the person was killed in action or died in the line of duty.

Article 6 (Notification of Decisions on Promotion)
(1) Where the Minister of National Defense makes a decision on whether to grant promotion pursuant to Article 5, notification thereof shall be given by means of a written decision on promotion in Attached Form 2.
(2) The Minister of National Defense shall notify the applicant of the written decision on promotion under paragraph (1) through the Chief of Staff of each service or Commandant of the Marine Corps.

Article 7 (Objections)
(1) A person who intends to file an objection pursuant to Article 6 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "objector") shall submit to the Minister of National Defense an objection in Attached Form 3, together with the following documents:
1. A certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register of the person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty, or a certified transcript of a removed family register (limited to cases where the relationship between the person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty and the objector cannot be verified through a certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register);
2. Other documents that can establish that the person for whom promotion is requested is a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty.
(2) Upon receiving an objection under paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall verify a certified copy of the objector's resident registration record through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the objector does not consent to verification, the Minister shall require the objector to attach that document.

Article 8 (Processing of Unique Identifying Information)
The Minister of National Defense, the Chief of Staff of each service, and the Commandant of the Marine Corps may process materials containing resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where it is unavoidable for the performance of affairs related to applications for promotion under Article 2, verification of facts under Article 3, decisions on promotion under Article 5, and objections under Article 7.

ADDENDUM <Presidential Decree No. 29994, 2019.7.23>

This Decree shall enter into force on July 24, 2019.
